absent_because.max_decompressed_bytes: this adapter accepts no compressed payload; HTTP content encoding is the caller's to undo, so there is no expansion to bound
absent_because.max_objects: not a bound this format needs: one file yields exactly three objects whatever it holds; the number of elements is bounded by max_input_bytes for octets and by MAX_POINTS = 200000 for every input (refused too-many-points before any element is read)
absent_because.max_parse_seconds: no wall-clock bound is enforced: this module reads no clock but the injected one, and the byte, depth and element bounds make every walk linear in a bounded input; the conformance suite's worker kills a decode that overruns its deadline

max_depth.enforced_at: the base class: `Adapter.__init_subclass__`'s wrapper calls `adapter.enforce_depth_bound` on the octets (read off the characters before json.loads) and on a parsed list (off its containers) before this class's `to_cdm` runs
max_depth.source: A track file nests two containers (the array and an element); an unknown key holding a structure can add more. 64 (`MAX_DEPTH`) is the harness loader's own bound and the figure synapse_cdm's JSON adapters declare. This is an IMPLEMENTATION CAP and is NOT the format's normative maximum.

max_input_bytes.enforced_at: `Adapter.__init_subclass__` wraps this class's own `to_cdm` with `enforce_input_bound` at class-definition time (`adapter.py`, `_bind_input_bound`), so the octets are measured and refused before this module decodes anything
max_input_bytes.source: The API documentation states no maximum response size. The largest real track file observed for one MMSI over one UTC day held a few thousand elements, roughly 1 MB at about 250 octets per element; 16 MiB (16 777 216 octets, `MAX_INPUT_BYTES`, `adapters/barentswatch_hais.py`) leaves an order of magnitude of headroom for a longer window. This is an IMPLEMENTATION CAP and is NOT the format's normative maximum.

message_types: BarentsWatch Historic AIS track response (GET /v1/historic/tracks/{mmsi}/{from}/{to}): one JSON array of position reports for one MMSI per call, as its UTF-8 octets or as the parsed list; one Entity, one Track and one TRACK_UPDATE Event per file
capabilities.unknown_fields_basis: the whole document, every element and every key in it, known or not, is the Entity's structured residual (`residual.data.points`, file order), and the names of keys outside the twelve the API is observed to write are listed at `attributes.unknown_keys`. The document is an ARRAY, so the conformance suite's check I, which injects keys into dict documents only, has no document to probe

limitations.summary: exactly one track response per call, for one MMSI, as UTF-8 octets or as the parsed list; JSON text as str, a dict and a batch of files are not taken. A file holding more than one MMSI is refused mixed-mmsi

nothing is joined across files: two windows of one vessel are two Tracks with one entity_id. A Track's and its Event's ids derive from the MMSI and the first and last sample instants, so two files spanning the same two instants give one track_id; the id names the vessel's window, not the file
the open BarentsWatch AIS data EXCLUDE fishing vessels under 15 m and leisure craft under 45 m, so an absent vessel or an empty window is not evidence that nothing was there

the historic API serves a limited retention window (the API documentation states 'No data older than 14 days', read 2026-10-22); older history is not retrievable through it, and this adapter states nothing about what lies outside the file

the provider filters satellite-received positions when a terrestrial one exists (`stream` names the receiving network); the file is the provider's selection, not every report that was transmitted, and a gap may be a filtered report

the API documentation does not establish whether rateOfTurn is the raw ROT_AIS integer or degrees per minute, so it is carried verbatim per sample and never converted; -128 is read as the AIS 'not available' value

TrackSample holds a position and an instant only, so each element's speed, course, heading, rate of turn, navigational status and stream ride in `attributes.barentswatch_samples` (arrays keyed by sample index) and the whole element in `residual.data.points[source_index]`; only the last sample's speed and course reach Entity.kinematics

the entity type is the ais adapter's MMSI rule and nothing else: a coast-station or aid-to-navigation MMSI (ais.MMSI_FACILITY_CATEGORIES) is a FACILITY whatever it transmits, every other MMSI is a PLATFORM, and the category is recorded at attributes.mmsi_category. A VIRTUAL aid to navigation, which the ais adapter reads from a type 21 message's own flag and types OVERLAY_OBJECT, cannot be told from a track file, so an aid-to-navigation MMSI here is always the physical FACILITY

the lossless ledger binds every source leaf to the residual and the MMSI to all three objects; it cannot express the time-order permutation from elements to samples, so the binding of latitude and longitude to Track.samples is proven by the adapter's tests, not by the ledger

every fixture is synthetic (MMSIs under the unallocated MID 299, as the ais fixtures use them, EX-prefixed names, positions inside CONTRIBUTING.md's Baltic rectangle); the shape follows the API's observed output, and no real response is part of the evidence
`evidence.available` is false because no published Release carries this adapter's records yet; it becomes true at the first release that attaches them

maturity.basis: L3 PROVENANCE VERIFIED, from evidence that runs today: `python -m synapse_cdm.harness --adapter barentswatch_hais` reports `translate`, `schema` and `provenance` PASS on every fixture, which carries L1 to L3, and its `lossless` column rests on the path-bound ledger (`MAPPINGS` declared, the whole document a structured residual on the Entity) with no LOST leaf. L4 is NOT declared: this adapter is ingest-only, so the roundtrip check is inapplicable rather than passed, and a rung passed vacuously is not a rung declared. Every fixture is synthetic; no real API response is part of the evidence.
